name: Real Madrid 1955-1960 (five European Cups)
scopeNote: From Real Madrid's first European Cup match (Servette 0-2 Real Madrid, Geneva, 8 September 1955) to the 1960 final (7-3 v Eintracht Frankfurt, Hampden Park, 18 May 1960). European seasons 1955/56 to 1959/60. Style label used by sources: W-M / 3-2-5 (3-2-2-3) with a roving deep centre-forward (Di Stefano); StatsBomb and Spielverlagerung say this, not 4-2-4 (a popular label for this side that no read source supports). Coaches in the period: Villalonga (1955/56, 1956/57), Carniglia (1957/58, 1958/59, with Munoz as interim Feb-Apr 1959), Fleitas Solich (1959/60 until April 1960), Munoz (from April 1960, coached the Hampden final). Most tactical coverage is retrospective (Spielverlagerung 2014, StatsBomb 2020, Holding Midfield 2012); no period source on the marking scheme was found. Day of Villalonga's departure and Carniglia's arrival not found (only June 1957, month level). Tactical evidence for 1955/56-1957/58 is thin: almost all of it concerns 1959/60 and the Di Stefano/Puskas partnership. Manager dates are month-level where marked partial: Villalonga end and Carniglia start 1957-06, Carniglia end 1959-07 (all from Wikipedia 'June 1957 to July 1959'), Fleitas start 1959-07 inferred from Carniglia's end and the 1959-60 season page; Fleitas end and Munoz start 1960-04-11 from Wikipedia's 1959-60 season page.
openQuestions: Who left Puskas out of the 1959 final? Wikipedia (Luis Carniglia) and SI say Carniglia left him out and was sacked in part for it; These Football Times says injury kept Puskas out of the 1959 final. Not resolved.

Fleitas Solich's last day: Wikipedia 1959-60 season says until 11 April 1960; a search summary of an Italian page (not read) said 17 April. Munoz's start is taken as 11 April 1960 from Wikipedia only. RSSSF coach list assigns 1959-60 wholly to Fleitas and 1960-61 to Munoz, but it is a season-level list and contradicts the three pages that put Munoz on the bench for the semi-finals and the final.

Villalonga's end and Carniglia's start: Wikipedia gives Carniglia from June 1957; RSSSF lists Jose A. Ipina and Carniglia for 1957-58. Villalonga's end date set to 1957-06 from this, not confirmed by a second source. Villalonga start (mid 1954-55 per Wikipedia) predates the period; clipped to 8 September 1955.

Marking scheme of Madrid itself (zonal or man) not found in any read page. StatsBomb only says the era was one of man-marking schemes and describes Frankfurt's Stein exploiting channels; treated as indirect evidence. No period source.
Spielverlagerung's 3-2-4-1/3-2-2-3 remark about Puskas is undated; eventDate set to 1959/60 as the first season Puskas started a final, not confirmed by the source.
Di Stefano's and Pachin's quotes are undated attributions; recorded in statedView as attributed with date unknown.
Set-pieces: nothing on corners or free kicks of this Madrid was found; only a kick-off move in the 1960 final is recorded.
The 7 coaches in 1955-1960 claimed by These Football Times does not match the four listed here; the extra names (for example Ipina, Munoz interim) were not checked further.
stated-view has no verified in-period fact: the only quotes found are undated or later attributions (statedView dates are article dates, not original dates).
